title: Direct identification through continuous biometric and location telemetry disclosure
description: By continuously providing heart rate patterns, GPS position, timestamps, and activity data to the wearable, the wearer may be directly identifiable or readily singled out, especially when the data is tied to a known device owner or account.
assumptions: The wearable is associated with a specific user account, device identifier, or otherwise attributable owner.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label for direct identifiability at disclosure may differ.

title: Linkability of telemetry records over time
description: The flow contains repeated sensor telemetry with timestamps and GPS position, enabling records from different moments to be linked to the same wearer and correlated into a longitudinal profile of movements, routines, and behavior.
assumptions: Telemetry is transmitted with stable device, session, or temporal characteristics sufficient to correlate records.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for linkability via repeated observations/identifiers may differ.

title: Inference of sensitive traits from raw sensor data
description: Even if the flow does not explicitly name the wearer, heart rate, step counts, GPS traces, and timestamps can allow inference of identity, home/work locations, daily routines, health status, exercise habits, religious attendance, or other sensitive attributes.
assumptions: The recipient or an attacker observing the flow can analyze combinations of telemetry fields over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for inference from observable data.

title: Identification of the wearer by the wearable device upon receipt
description: Once the wearable receives and processes continuous telemetry, it may associate the data with a persistent device identity, paired phone, or user profile, making the wearer identifiable within the system.
assumptions: The device maintains persistent identifiers, pairing state, or user profiles.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact destination-side identifiability node may differ.

title: Linking current telemetry with historical observations
description: The wearable can combine newly captured telemetry with prior measurements to build a continuous history of the same wearer, linking sessions and contexts over long periods.
assumptions: The device stores or otherwise correlates telemetry across time.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for destination-side linkability may differ.

title: Inference of health, habits, and location patterns by device processing
description: Processing the incoming telemetry allows the wearable to derive higher-level information such as fitness level, sleep/wake cycles, stress episodes, commuting routes, home/work addresses, and other sensitive patterns not explicitly provided by the wearer.
assumptions: The device software performs analytics or stores sufficient data for later analysis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for inference at the destination.

title: Unawareness of continuous collection scope
description: The wearer may not fully understand that wearing the device continuously captures multiple sensor streams, including precise location and timestamps, and that this occurs persistently rather than only during active use.
assumptions: Notices or UI indicators are limited, unclear, or absent.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for unawareness about collection/processing may differ.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive or insufficiently justified collection
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps may exceed what is necessary for a given purpose, or may lack a valid legal basis, transparency, or appropriate safeguards, creating a privacy non-compliance threat.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require purpose limitation, data minimization, transparency, and lawful basis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for non-compliance related to over-collection and transparency.
